claims.claim: Ordered-bipartition criterion: a bipartite n-vertex tree with classes A={x1,...,xa} and B={y1,...,yb} has a bipartition-separated graceful labeling if and only if the two classes can be ordered so that the endpoint-rank sums i+j over edges xiyj are pairwise distinct.
claims.evidence: Since a+b=n, every endpoint-rank sum lies in {2,...,n}; the n−1 edge sums are pairwise distinct exactly when they equal this whole set. Given such orders, phi(x_i)=i and phi(y_j)=n+1−j use every label once and give difference n+1−i−j, hence differences 1,...,n−1. Conversely, complement first if B is the lower class. Then a separated labeling gives A exactly labels 1,...,a and B exactly a+1,...,n; ordering A increasingly and B decreasingly recovers the same formula and distinct rank sums.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional algebraic proof for arbitrary bipartition sizes.

claims.claim: For every caterpillar, the bipartition orders described in the final writeup give endpoint-rank sums 2,3,...,n in succession.
claims.evidence: The first leaf edge has sum 2. Within each leaf block the moving endpoint’s rank increases by one; the next spine vertex immediately follows that block in its class; and after a spine edge the next leaf block immediately follows the preceding spine vertex in the other class. Thus every successive listed edge raises the sum by one, including across empty blocks. There are n−1 edges, so the sums end at n. The checker confirmed the construction on all 4,224 caterpillars among the generated trees through order 15.
claims.search_method: General rank induction, supplemented by exact exhaustive testing through order 15.
claims.witness: All 4,224 generated caterpillars through order 15 passed the consecutive-rank-sum and graceful-label validators.

claims.evidence: Claims 0 and 1 give the explicit graceful labeling phi(x_i)=i and phi(y_j)=n+1−j. The one- and two-vertex cases are immediate. The checker independently validated the constructed labeling for every generated caterpillar through order 15.
claims.search_method: Deduction from the proved rank criterion and caterpillar order construction, with finite exhaustive validation.
claims.witness: The explicit labeling is phi(x_i)=i and phi(y_j)=n+1−j for the stated bipartition orders.

claims.claim: Extreme-vertex leaf-extension lemma: if a graceful n-vertex tree has a vertex v labeled 1, attaching any s≥0 new leaves at v preserves gracefulness.
claims.evidence: A graceful n-vertex tree has old differences exactly 1,...,n−1. Retain its labels and assign the new leaves n+1,...,n+s. Their edges to the vertex labeled 1 have differences n,...,n+s−1, disjoint from the old differences, and all labels 1,...,n+s occur exactly once. This also covers s=0.
claims.search_method: Direct symbolic construction for arbitrary s.

claims.claim: For every r≥0, the tree obtained from the once-subdivided K1,3 by adjoining r additional leaves to its center is a graceful non-caterpillar.
claims.evidence: With center c=1 and (u_i,w_i)=(7,3),(6,5),(4,2), the original six differences are 6,4,5,1,3,2. Labeling the r added center-leaves 8,...,7+r supplies differences 7,...,6+r, so every required difference occurs once. Removing the leaves leaves the induced K1,3 on c,u1,u2,u3, not a path, so every member is non-caterpillar. The checker validated all instances within its supported orders.
claims.search_method: Uniform explicit construction for arbitrary r, supplemented by exact validation for r=0,...,8.
claims.witness: c=1; (u1,w1)=(7,3), (u2,w2)=(6,5), (u3,w3)=(4,2); added leaf z_t has label 7+t for 1≤t≤r.

claims.claim: The once-subdivided K1,3 has no bipartition-separated graceful labeling; hence not every tree admits the stronger alpha-type labeling used for caterpillars.
claims.evidence: After complementation if necessary, A={c,w1,w2,w3} is lower. If c has rank r, its three edge sums are r+1,r+2,r+3. For r=1, producing leaf sum 7 forces ranks (4,3), leaving maximum remaining sum 5 rather than 6. For r=4, sum 2 forces (1,1), leaving minimum 4 rather than 3. For r=2, sums 2 and 7 force (1,1) and (4,3), leaving 3+2=5 rather than 6. For r=3, the same extremes leave 2+2=4 rather than 3. The checker independently exhausted all 4!·3!=144 orders and found none.
claims.search_method: Complete four-case center-rank proof and exhaustive enumeration of all bipartition orders.
claims.witness: The graph has edges c-u_i and u_i-w_i for i=1,2,3; zero of its 144 ordered-bipartition pairs have distinct endpoint-rank sums.

claims.claim: The checker’s inductive generator contains exactly one representative of every unlabeled tree at each tested order.
claims.evidence: Deleting a leaf from any tree proves inductively that attaching a leaf at every vertex of every preceding representative is surjective onto the next order. Equality of sorted recursive child codes is equivalent, by induction, to rooted-tree isomorphism. Rooting at the unique center, or sorting the two rooted half-codes at a central edge, is therefore a complete invariant of free trees. Deduplication by this code retains exactly one representative. The generated counts matched the stated sequence at every order.
claims.search_method: Inductive leaf-attachment enumeration with complete center-rooted canonical coding and duplicate-code assertions.

claims.claim: For n≥2, in searching for a graceful labeling, it is complete to guess an edge, give its endpoints labels 0 and n−1 in one orientation, and search the remaining labels.
claims.evidence: There are n−1 distinct positive edge differences, each at most n−1, so a graceful labeling must use every difference 1,...,n−1. Difference n−1 occurs only between labels 0 and n−1, hence those labels occupy an edge. Complementing every label by n−1−x preserves all differences and reverses that edge’s orientation, so one fixed orientation per candidate edge is complete.
claims.search_method: Extremal-difference proof; the checker retains an uncapped one-orientation-per-edge completeness pass.

claims.claim: The persisted backtracking and validation procedure is exact: every reported witness is graceful, and its pruning rules cannot remove a possible completion.
claims.evidence: The assigned vertices start with an edge and remain connected. An unassigned boundary vertex therefore has exactly one assigned neighbor, since two would form a cycle. For the selected boundary vertex the search exhausts every free label whose parent-edge difference is unused. Every genuine completion follows one such branch. Failure of an individual difference-to-unresolved-edge feasibility test, or of the stronger Hall matching used by the checker, is necessary for failure because any completion induces such a matching. Bounded probes only change scheduling and are followed by an uncapped exhaustive pass. Every returned labeling is separately checked to use exactly labels 0,...,n−1 and differences 1,...,n−1.
claims.search_method: Code-path audit plus complete-search invariant and necessary-pruning proofs; full exact execution through order 15.
claims.witness: The completed run returned and independently revalidated 13,188 witnesses without a validation failure.

claims.claim: Every tree on at most 15 vertices is graceful.
claims.evidence: The complete canonical generator supplies one representative of every isomorphism class through order 15, and the exact run produced a validated graceful labeling for each representative. Transporting a labeling through an isomorphism and adding one to every 0-based label yields the target convention {1,...,n}.
claims.search_method: Deduction from the proved generator completeness and independently reproduced finite certificate.
claims.witness: All 13,188 isomorphism representatives through order 15 were certified.

claims.claim: Any counterexample to the graceful tree conjecture must have at least 16 vertices and contain a vertex adjacent to at least three non-leaf vertices.
claims.evidence: Claim 10 excludes orders at most 15, while Claim 2 excludes caterpillars. In any tree with at least three vertices, the vertices of degree at least two induce a connected subtree: every internal vertex on a path between two such vertices also has degree at least two. If every vertex had at most two neighbors in this induced subtree, it would be a connected tree of maximum degree at most two, hence a path, making the original tree a caterpillar. The contrapositive proves the claimed local obstruction. The checker also confirmed this equivalence on all generated trees.
claims.search_method: Structural contrapositive proof, supplemented by exhaustive verification on all 13,188 generated trees.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a proof that every finite tree is graceful or an explicit finite nongraceful tree with a rigorous impossibility proof. The draft supplies neither and explicitly says that arbitrary unbounded non-caterpillar trees remain unsettled. It does rigorously establish gracefulness for all caterpillars, an infinite graceful non-caterpillar family, every tree through order 15, and necessary conditions on any counterexample. These are substantive but incomplete results, so the target verdict is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. Because the draft claims only PARTIAL and expressly disclaims a universal resolution or counterexample, claimed_resolution is ACCURATE and the final writeup does not overclaim.
